gist: Anthony Pompliano and Jordi Visser argue the next 12 months belong to crypto over AI-infrastructure names: with Bitcoin consolidating near $80K and the 200-day MAs on BTC and ETH turning up, Visser has rotated more capital into BTC/ETH/SOL on the thesis that 'agentic applications' need on-chain financial guardrails (stablecoins for transactions, Bitcoin as collateral, tokenization for illiquid assets) and that big money 'hasn't done the homework' yet — his Micron-style setup. He reads Warsh's Jackson Hole speech as noise against Bessent's revealed preference for lower long-end yields (yen intervention, TGA, debt buybacks, stablecoins as treasury buyers) to 'run it hot' and let AI/humanoids outgrow the debt, and frames NVIDIA's blowout as scarcity-driven and un-dot-com-like, with a $700T-assets math sketching Bitcoin toward $600K-$1M.

insights.claim: Bitcoin is consolidating a historic multi-standard-deviation move near $80K, with 82K as natural resistance and 74K (near the 200-day MA) the support that matters most; the 200-day MAs on both Bitcoin and Ethereum have turned upward, a setup that historically precedes strong forward returns once price breaks back above and the MA turns up.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The technical structure (rising 200-day MA reclaim) is Visser's evidence the crypto move is early-stage, not late; 74K and 82K are the levels to trade around.
insights.quote: now we have the 200-day moving average pointed upward in both the Ethereum and Bitcoin

insights.claim: Visser has shifted more capital into crypto (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana) than into AI-infrastructure names, on the thesis that the next year is about agentic applications requiring on-chain 'financial guardrails' for agent transactions, while still expecting AI-infra names to beat the S&P over 12 months.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A concrete allocation tilt: crypto (esp. ETH/SOL for network effects and tokenization) over AI infra for the next 12 months, driven by agent-payment rails rather than Bitcoin alone.
insights.quote: I have more money focused on crypto right now and it's not just Bitcoin. It's Ethereum. It's Solana.

insights.claim: Ethereum has broken out versus Bitcoin and Solana has outperformed Ethereum recently (Solana +50% month-to-date, its biggest monthly move since 2024), which Visser reads as fundamentally-driven rotation that will pull traditional-finance investors in, unlike the meme-coin (Dogecoin) moves he dismisses as GameStop-like retail signals.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: ETH>BTC and SOL>ETH leadership is the 'fundamentally driven' tell to watch; meme-coin outperformance is noise, not signal.
insights.quote: Solana was up 50% month to date and was the biggest monthly move since 2024

insights.claim: Crypto is a 'homework not done yet' trade analogous to Micron early last year (60 to 110 to eventually 1,300): the large money managers Visser talks to are deeply versed on NVIDIA but 'nowhere' on tokenization, stablecoins and payment rails, and he expects them to be focused on Solana/Ethereum by year-end.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The edge thesis: outsized (3-10x) returns come from areas institutions haven't researched yet; the window is roughly January through August next year before the crowd arrives.
insights.quote: I don't think people have done the homework yet, the same way they didn't do the homework on the AI infrastructure trade

insights.claim: South Korea's retail base is rotating from the AI trade back into crypto (volumes 'exploding'), with Bitcoin visibly popping around the Korean market open; Korea's stock market is still up 60%+ despite margin-liquidation stories, supplying the retail 'energy' that is the first phase of a crypto move.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Korean retail flow (and the Korean-open Bitcoin bid) is a near-term momentum indicator, though Visser says retail alone can't sustain the move without fundamental/institutional buyers.
insights.quote: volumes are starting to explode in Korea on crypto

insights.claim: Visser reads Warsh's Jackson Hole speech as showmanship for Fed credibility that said nothing that matters (about 40% odds of a September hike still priced), because the revealed policy is Bessent's: he keeps jawboning long-end yields down (yen intervention, using the TGA, expanded debt buybacks) roughly every three days, and Warsh is unlikely to hike in September and offset that.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Trade the actions, not the speech: the administration's persistent effort to suppress long-end yields is the dominant force, making a surprise September hike unlikely.
insights.quote: he's talked about using the TGA to get rates down. He's talked about debt buybacks... it almost seems like every 3 days he's jawboning to try and get long-term rates down

insights.claim: The core administration bet is to run the economy hot and let humanoids and AI agents create GDP faster than debt rises, with Visser predicting higher future corporate taxes (funded by humanoid-driven margins) to help pay down the debt.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Frames fiscal policy as an explicit AI-growth wager; if it works, equity terminal values (3-5 years out) justify today's compressed PEs despite the debt, and higher corporate taxes become the eventual repayment mechanism.
insights.quote: we're going to run it hot and we're going to try to have the humanoids and the AI agents create more GDP at a faster pace than the debt is going to rise

insights.claim: Druckenmiller's AI-written op-ed attacked Congress (a 6% deficit and $40T debt), not Bessent, and Visser argues policymakers have little choice: with equities at ~240% heading toward 300% of GDP and a wealth-distribution problem driving socialist voting, letting 10-year yields rise to 5.5% would 'open Pandora's box,' so rates are being held below the ~6% nominal-GDP level fundamentals imply.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Explains why long yields are structurally suppressed despite ~6% nominal GDP; the fiscal fragility caps how high rates can go, supporting the debasement/scarcity trade.
insights.quote: The stock market is 240% on its way to 300% of GDP... I don't think having long-term yields go up to 5 and 1/2% is going to change that.

insights.claim: Stablecoins will be almost entirely dollar-based because the majority of the world faces currency debasement, and Bessent's plan connects to crypto: keep the basis trade going, deregulate banks to buy more treasuries, and grow stablecoins toward $3 trillion so they too buy treasuries, buying time for AI to grow out of the debt problem.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Positions dollar stablecoins as an emerging structural buyer of Treasuries (a ~$3T potential bid) and a policy tool, linking crypto adoption directly to US debt financing.
insights.quote: we need stablecoins to be up to $3 trillion so they can buy treasuries as well. All to let the humanoids and the speed of AI get us out of this problem.

insights.claim: NVIDIA is now doing over $1 billion of revenue per day and guiding ~70% revenue growth next year well above the street, with 2028 earnings around $20 on a $220 stock, the opposite of the dot-com bubble where Cisco traded at 100x PE.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The falling forward PE against 70%-plus guided growth is the bull's rebuttal to circular-finance bears; NVIDIA is not a 100x-PE Cisco analog.
insights.quote: we're talking about 70% rev next year... for 2028 they've got $20 for earnings on a $220 stock

insights.claim: Citing the Dwarkesh Patel / Dylan Patel conversation, Visser argues compute demand will never be satisfied and that OpenAI and Anthropic have such high margins on superior intelligence that they can pay for all incoming compute, pointing toward a potential compute near-monopoly and explaining why both are moving toward going public.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: If OpenAI/Anthropic can absorb all available compute on margin, they concentrate the AI value chain; their IPOs become a way to fund that compute dominance.
insights.quote: these guys alone are going to be the ones that need all of the compute

insights.claim: NVIDIA is up only ~25% over the past year despite ~100% growth because of ownership saturation, opportunity cost (a ~$5T cap, nearly 2x the entire crypto market, needs enormous marginal dollars to move), and the terminal-value/scarcity question: NVIDIA has scarcity now but won't in 5-6 years, which would compress its discounted-cash-flow value.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Reframes NVIDIA's muted stock as a size/scarcity-duration problem, not a growth problem; the key variable is how long true GPU scarcity lasts before efficiency and competition erode terminal value.
insights.quote: at some point, five years from now, six years from now, it won't have scarcity, the value of Nvidia is the total sum of the future discounted cash flows

insights.claim: OpenAI's AI-designed Jalapeno chip (built with Broadcom) won't disrupt NVIDIA's numbers this year or next, but raises whether NVIDIA's CUDA/design moat erodes once humanoids scale and algorithmic efficiencies reduce compute needs, though Visser sees another 3-5 years of heavy compute demand.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Custom AI-designed silicon is a multi-year threat to NVIDIA's moat, not an immediate one; the 3-5 year heavy-compute runway is the window before efficiency/competition bite.

insights.claim: Visser dismisses 'debasement' as merely a narrative and frames the real driver as scarcity: Bitcoin and gold are the two chosen scarcity assets (correlation at its highest ever), with Bitcoin the digital store of value and gold the traditional one, both bid as AI-driven abundance destroys value elsewhere.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Positions BTC and gold as the scarcity pair to own against AI abundance; the record BTC-gold correlation suggests they trade as one 'scarcity' allocation.
insights.quote: I believe this is about scarcity... those are the two assets are the definitions of scarcity

insights.claim: In the on-chain stack, stablecoins are the transaction layer (what Bitcoin couldn't do), Bitcoin is collateral/store-of-value, and tokenization lets illiquid assets (IP, private cash flows) move on-chain in real time; Coinbase's Bitcoin-backed mortgages exemplify Bitcoin as liquid, real-time collateral versus illiquid income/job assumptions.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A clean layered thesis for allocating within crypto: stablecoins = payments, Bitcoin = collateral, ETH/SOL = tokenization infrastructure; Bitcoin-collateralized lending (mortgages) is a concrete growth vector.
insights.quote: Stablecoins are the transaction side. Bitcoin is absolutely collateral. It is a store of value.

insights.claim: Visser's Bitcoin price framework: if ~$700T of global assets require on-chain 'financial guardrails' worth ~$100T in the future and Bitcoin stays ~33% of crypto (~$33T) from ~$2T today, that implies a 10-15x move to roughly $600K-$1M per Bitcoin over the next decade.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A back-of-envelope path to $600K-$1M Bitcoin driven by asset migration to on-chain rails; Pompliano notes Bitcoin is already 50%+ (arguably 75-80% ex-scams) of crypto market cap, which would push the number higher.
insights.quote: at 4 trillion, that number to me has to be 100 trillion in the future... let's assume it ends up being 33% of crypto, well then you're talking about 33 trillion

insights.claim: Trust beats best-innovation in the merging of old and new financial systems: every major bank and exchange is pursuing tokenization (Japan targeting fully on-chain by ~2030) and institutions keep naming Ethereum and Solana, implying Mag-7-style concentration within crypto where trust, not superior tech, decides winners.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Concentration bet within crypto: ETH and Solana are favored not for best technology but for institutional trust and mindshare, the analog to owning the Mag 7 over the other 493.
insights.quote: the trust for merging is going to be very important to the final decision, not the best innovation
